content: 1. Acycline increases the level or effect of neratinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors should not be coadministered with neratinib. 2. Tetracycline decreases the level or effect of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 3. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of nirogacestat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of norgestrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. 5. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of olaparib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 6. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of oliceridine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 7. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of omaveloxolone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 8. Tetracycline decreases the effects of oxacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 9. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of pacritinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of palbociclib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of palovarotene by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. Systemic retinoid use has been associated with benign intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri), particularly with concomitant tetracycline use. 12. Tetracycline increases the effects of pancuronium due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 13. Tetracycline decreases the level or effect of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 14. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of pemigatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pemigatinib dose may be resumed. 15. Tetracycline decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 16. Tetracycline decreases the effects of penicillin VK due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of pexidartinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed. 18. Tetracycline increases the effects of phenindione due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 19. Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 20. Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Tetracycline decreases the effects of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 22. Polycarbophil decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Polysaccharide iron decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of porfimer due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely due to enhanced photosensitivity. 25. Primidone decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Tetracycline increases the effects of protamine due to pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 27. Tetracycline decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 28. Tetracycline increases the effects of rapacuronium due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 29. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait three to five elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 30. Rifabutin decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Rifapentine decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of rimegepant by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 34. Tetracycline increases the effects of rocuronium due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 35. Rose hips decrease tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, tetracycline decreases rose hips levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 36. Rucaparib increases the level or effect of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 37. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of ruxolitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of seladelpar by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, particularly in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are coadministered a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 39. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of selumetinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. 40. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of siponimod by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 41. Sodium bicarbonate decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by two hours. 42. Sodium citrate/citric acid decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by two hours. 43. Tetracycline decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Additionally, sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid decreases tetracycline levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer tetracycline at least two hours before and not less than six hours after administration of sodium picosulfate, magnesium oxide, and anhydrous citric acid to avoid magnesium chelation. 44. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least two hours before and not less than six hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 45. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Administer tetracyclines at least two hours before and not less than six hours after each dose to avoid chelation with magnesium. 46. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of sonidegib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, administer it for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse reactions. 47. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of sparsentan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is needed. Regularly monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function if sparsentan is coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Stiripentol affects tetracycline metabolism by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 49. Strontium ranelate decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Coadministration is contraindicated. Suspend strontium ranelate during antibiotic therapy. 50. Tetracycline increases the effects of succinylcholine due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug due to the risk of respiratory depression. 51. Sucralfate decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 52. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of sufentanil SL by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of sufentanil SL with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, potentially leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. 53. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of suvorexant by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Decrease the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of tadalafil by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce tadalafil clearance, increasing systemic exposure and the risk of associated adverse events. 55. Tazemetostat decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Tetracycline also increases the level or effect of tazemetostat by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per the drug monograph. 56. Tecovirimat decreases the level or effect of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 57. Tetracycline decreases the effects of temocillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 58. Tetracycline increases the level or effect of tezacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
